chunks.title: EC2 Instance IAM Role — SSM Access and Scoped S3 Read
chunks.content:
EC2 Instance IAM Role — SSM Access and Scoped S3 Read

Creates an IAM role assumable by the EC2 service, exposed to instances through an aws_iam_instance_profile. The role attaches the AWS-managed AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy (enabling Systems Manager Session Manager) and a custom inline-built policy granting s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on a single named application bucket.

When to use:
- Use to give an EC2 workload read access to one specific S3 bucket without embedding long-lived credentials on the instance
- Use the SSM managed policy to enable Session Manager so administrators do not need SSH (port 22) open to the instance

Best practices:
- Attach permissions to EC2 via an instance profile, not by placing access keys on the host
- Prefer SSM Session Manager over opening port 22 for shell access — it replaces SSH and leaves an auditable trail
- Namespace roles with a path (e.g. /app/) and tag them (Environment, ManagedBy=terraform) for organization and cleanup

Security considerations:
- Scope the S3 policy to the explicit bucket ARN and its objects (arn:aws:s3:::<bucket> and /*) rather than Resource: "*" — this is least privilege
- Grant only the actions the workload needs (read-only GetObject/ListBucket here), not s3:*

Terraform resources: aws_iam_role ec2_app (assume_role_policy Principal Service=ec2.amazonaws.com) + aws_iam_instance_profile + aws_iam_role_policy_attachment to AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore + aws_iam_policy ec2_s3_read (s3:GetObject/ListBucket scoped to var.app_bucket_name).

chunks.title: CI/CD IAM Role via GitHub Actions OIDC — No Static Keys
chunks.content:
CI/CD IAM Role via GitHub Actions OIDC — No Static Keys

Creates an IAM role that GitHub Actions assumes through OIDC federation using sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity against the token.actions.githubusercontent.com OIDC provider. Trust is constrained by a StringLike condition on the token `sub` (repo:my-org/my-repo:*) and a StringEquals condition on `aud` (sts.amazonaws.com). The attached policy grants ECR push/pull actions scoped to the environment's repository path.

When to use:
- Use for CI/CD pipelines that deploy to AWS so the pipeline authenticates via short-lived OIDC tokens instead of long-lived IAM user access keys
- Use when the pipeline must push container images to ECR and pull them back during deploy

Best practices:
- Prefer OIDC web-identity federation over storing static AWS access keys in CI secrets — there are no long-lived credentials to rotate or leak
- Scope the ECR object actions (BatchCheckLayerAvailability, PutImage, UploadLayerPart, BatchGetImage, GetDownloadUrlForLayer, etc.) to the specific repository ARN path (repository/${var.environment}/*)

Security considerations:
- Restrict the trust policy `sub` to your exact org/repo (repo:my-org/my-repo:*) — never use "*", which would let any GitHub repo assume the role
- ecr:GetAuthorizationToken requires Resource "*" by API design; keep all other ECR actions scoped to the repository path so a token leak cannot reach unrelated repositories

Terraform resources: data.aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.github + aws_iam_role github_actions_deploy (AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, StringLike sub, StringEquals aud) + aws_iam_policy github_actions_ecr (GetAuthorizationToken on *, other ECR actions scoped to repository/${env}/*).

chunks.title: EKS Worker Node IAM Role — Required Managed Policies
chunks.content:
EKS Worker Node IAM Role — Required Managed Policies

Creates an IAM role assumable by the EC2 service for EKS worker nodes and attaches the three AWS-managed policies EKS nodes require: AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy (node registration), AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy (VPC CNI pod networking), and AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly (pull images from ECR).

When to use:
- Use as the instance role for EKS managed or self-managed worker nodes that must join the cluster, run the VPC CNI, and pull images from ECR

Best practices:
- Attach exactly the three required managed policies (worker node, CNI, ECR read-only) — these are the documented minimum for nodes to function

Security considerations:
- Permissions on the node role apply to every pod scheduled on the node; use IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts) to grant application-specific AWS permissions at the pod level instead of broadening this node role

Terraform resources: aws_iam_role eks_node (assume by ec2.amazonaws.com) + role_policy_attachments to AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy, AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly.
